review.editorial_summary: Completed a Python MARC21 implementation with rules extracted from the supplied corpus; the unchanged source passes all 2,900 corrected tests.
review.notes:
The preserved transcript and authored source show a voluntary completion, 41 self-tests and Python 3.11 syntax checks. The program implements all four actions with shared validation and separate ISO/MARCXML codecs, and bundles its extracted rules with a regeneration utility. Its original 2,883/2,900 grade contained 17 fixture failures: four undersized 007 examples whose normative requirement is ambiguous, twelve flattened or contradictory 018/357/880 examples, and one positive empty-subfield fixture violating unrelated Directory ordering. Version 3.0.2 repairs the positive contexts using the public text and leaves both acceptance and rejection of undersized 007 c/m records unscored. No submission defect remains in these 2,900 cases. Original source, transcript, grade and usage remain preserved; the Docker regrade used no model inference and added no model cost. Recorded token, reasoning, cache and tool counts were reparsed from preserved telemetry. Docker egress and actual hosted-tool use are audited separately, with conditions attached to the comparison cohort.

Run conditions: apps available but no external tool invocation observed.
